ground_alt_m.description: ground height at the origin above sea level, or "auto" to look it up

heading_deg.description: the way the start pads face

pads.description: where vehicles start; the first is player 1's

from_deg.description: where it blows from, degrees true

turbulence.description: MIL-F-8785C's turbulence for this wind (σ_w 0.1 × the wind at 6 m) times this: 0 smooth air, 1 the standard's, 2 and 3 as rough as its moderate and severe

eddy_scale.description: the turbulence's scale lengths times this: larger is slower, rolling air; 1 is MIL-F-8785C's

gust_factor.description: the strongest gust over the mean wind, as a weather report gives it; 1: no gusts on top of the turbulence

SessionMsg.description:
Start a vehicle at a location, switch vehicle (back at the start), reset, destroy (a
crash: the physics stops dead), throw (a hand-launched wing), or stop. A start may fit a
payload (content/payloads: Shoot Down's charge) to the vehicle; a switch keeps it. A start
at a place of the player's own (the menu's GPS point) carries it whole, as `place`.

payload.description: start: a payload to fit, its id

place.description: start: a place not in the content (a GPS point typed in the menu), whose id is `location`

SessionMsg.title: SessionMsg

RcMsg.description: The radio's channels, from channel 1, µs (1000-2000).
RcMsg.title: RcMsg

GroundMsg.description: The ground's height above sea level under the vehicle, from the map's 3D tiles.
GroundMsg.title: GroundMsg

WindMsg.description: The wind now (the Wind options tab); `gust_now` starts a gust at once (G).
WindMsg.title: WindMsg

DynamicsMsg.description: Stream the flight model's internals (the dynamics overlay) or stop.
DynamicsMsg.title: DynamicsMsg

RadioSourceMsg.description:
Read the radio in the server (Linux evdev) and stream it here (RadioMsg), for when
Chrome's Gamepad API cannot see all of it; or stop. `fly`: the server flies it straight to
the firmware (rc.pilot), and the page sends no `rc` (DESIGN.md §12).
RadioSourceMsg.title: RadioSourceMsg

TargetMsg.description:
Fly the session's quad itself, for a target to shoot at: "hover" takes off from its pad
and holds `height_m` above it, or climbs or sinks to it if already up; "land" lands where it
is. ArduCopter is flown as a ground station would (GUIDED, armed over MAVLink, a takeoff;
LAND), with an idle receiver played (firmware/ardupilot.py); Betaflight, which takes no such
commands, as a pilot on its switches would (POSHOLD; firmware/betaflight.py). The page sends
no `rc` meanwhile.

"go" (ArduCopter, up and in GUIDED after a hover) flies it on, a target the page sends a few
times a second: to a point on a path (`lat`, `lon`, `height_m`), with `vel_ned` as where it
is going next; facing `yaw_deg` if given. Straight to the firmware, not queued behind other
commands.

"path" (Betaflight, up after a hover) flies `points` (lat, lon) at `height_m`, round and
round, as a mission its own autopilot flies (firmware/betaflight.py), sent once; a hover
or a land takes it back. Straight to the firmware too.

height_m.description: above the pad, m: hover's (2 at least), go's

vel_ned.description: go: the path's velocity there, m/s, north, east, down

points.description: path: its waypoints, lat and lon, degrees

TargetMsg.title: TargetMsg

HitMsg.description:
A bullet struck the vehicle, as the page traced it: which part, and the momentum it left.
The physics takes what the part did away (physics/quad/model.py: an arm, that rotor; the
body, the power at once; the pack, the power a moment later; the payload goes off) and the
impulse at the point it struck; the firmware flies on with what is left.

motor.description: ArduPilot's motor number (1 front right, 2 rear left, 3 front left, 4 rear right) for an arm; None otherwise

impulse_ned.description: the momentum the bullet leaves in the vehicle, N·s, north, east, down

at_frd.description: where it struck, m from the centre of mass, body forward, right, down

HitMsg.title: HitMsg

PayloadSpec.description:
A charge strapped under a quad (Shoot Down fits it, whichever quad: content/payloads):
carried as part of its mass, drawn under it, a part a bullet can hit. Hit, or (one time in
two) when the quad comes down on the ground after a hit, it goes off
(physics/quad/model.py).

size_m.description: a tube along the quad, forward: its length and diameter

below_m.description: its axis below the quad's centre of mass

lethal_m.description: within this of where it goes off, a person is killed

PayloadSpec.title: PayloadSpec

step.description: what starting is doing now, or why it failed

origin.description: the pad: lat, lon, ground m above sea level

TelemetryMsg.description:
What a ground station sees, from MAVLink (ArduPilot) or MSP (INAV): the map and the dials
read this, never the physics (DESIGN.md §2.2).
TelemetryMsg.title: TelemetryMsg

OsdMsg.description: The firmware's own OSD screen, as MSP DisplayPort drew it: character codes row by row.
OsdMsg.title: OsdMsg

PlanMsg.description: The vehicle's uploaded mission, fence and rally points (ArduPilot).
PlanMsg.title: PlanMsg

LogMsg.description: A line from the firmware (STATUSTEXT) or the session.
LogMsg.title: LogMsg

RadioMsg.description:
The radio as the server reads it: every axis, -1..1, nothing reversed, and the channels
as the server maps them (its profile, the player's calibration); name None with no radio. At
60 Hz while a page asks (RadioSourceMsg).
RadioMsg.title: RadioMsg

Damage.description: What hits have taken from the quad so far (HitMsg).

lost.description: each motor's (1-4, ArduPilot's) rotor shot away: its arm, motor or prop hit (the page stops drawing its prop)

power.description: the motors' power: a body hit cuts it at once (off); a pierced pack holds a moment (failing), then off

exploded.description: its payload has gone off: the quad is gone

hits.description: hits taken since the last reset

Damage.title: Damage

PhysicsMsg.description:
What the physics says the vehicle is doing, on each change: "ground", "hand", "flying",
"crashed"; whether its firmware is stepping it; and what hits have taken from it.
PhysicsMsg.title: PhysicsMsg

AuxSpec.description: What the firmware does on each AUX channel (channel numbers 5-16).

modes.description: the mode switch's positions, low to high

AuxSpec.title: AuxSpec

offset_m.description: forward, right, down of the CG

Cartridge.description:
The round a weapon fires: what the ballistics (web/src/shoot/ballistics.ts) and the recoil
(web/src/shoot/recoil.ts) need of it.

length_mm.description: the bullet's length, mm (its spin stability)

muzzle_ms.description: muzzle speed from this weapon's barrel, m/s

powder_g.description: the powder charge, g: its gas recoils too

tracer_every.description: a tracer every this many rounds as loaded; 0: none (the menu may change it)

Cartridge.title: Cartridge

match.description: substrings of the Gamepad API id ('Vendor: 1209 Product: 4f54') that pick this profile

params.description: parameter / CLI files, relative to firmware/

alt_m.description: the gate's centre, m above the ground or sea (alt_ref)

GateFrame.description: The course's gate: a square frame round the inside that is flown through.

inside_m.description: width, height of the way through

outside_m.description: width, height of the whole frame

depth_m.description: the frame's thickness along the way through

GateFrame.title: GateFrame

Payload.description: A payload a mode fits to the vehicle it starts (content/payloads/*.toml).

size_m.description: a tube along the quad, forward: its length and diameter

below_m.description: its axis below the quad's centre of mass

lethal_m.description: within this of where it goes off, a person is killed

params.description: parameter / CLI files, after the vehicle's, for a firmware that carries it

Payload.title: Payload

airframe.description: the model's airframe id (racer5in, chupito, truck)

model.description: the 3D model, under web/public/models or a /vendor path

payload.description: fitted by the session (a start's payload, content/payloads), not in its file

twist_in.description: the rifling's turn, inches per turn, right hand

sights.description: the sights it has, the first fitted

zero_m.description: the range its sights are zeroed at, m
